saying:
Nearly all commenters accept comparing devices to the care patients would otherwise get
informationally
unaided clinicians, delayed specialist review, or no intervention
but want the counterfactual prespecified, empirically demonstrated for the deployment setting, and carried into labeling, with device-alone and human-AI team results reported separately. Several add an absolute safety floor so weak local baselines are not entrenched.

disagreement.text: Commenters split on whether beating the actual counterfactual is enough. Some say devices outperforming existing care should not face higher hurdles than that care; others say improvement over prevailing practice must be paired with an evidence-based standard or absolute safety floor, and reject median or local practice as the benchmark.

sides.summary: Care actually available absent the device is the appropriate benchmark; do not hold devices to a standard the delivery system itself does not meet.
Counterfactual comparison must be supplemented by an evidence-based clinical standard or absolute safety floor so substandard baselines are not normalized.
